risk_findings.why: Several short reports mention blood, damage, a stuck door, smoke, or entrapment without establishing a person is injured/inside/trapped. Preserve uncertainty; object damage or scene clues alone should not imply a person-level severity.

Negation may describe no injury, no breathing, inability, absent people, or inability to locate someone. The scope and experiencer differ and require fluent annotation; keyword polarity cannot determine severity.

Nonresponse can mean unconscious/unresponsive after direct observation, or merely no reply to a text/call; fatality words may be hearsay or ambiguous. Separate physical consciousness and breathing from digital communication failure.

risk_findings.risk: Ambiguous / unsupported label from very short text
risk_findings.why: 54 rows contain only 1?3 words; 34 are needs_review, while critical has 5 and serious 8. Many omit person condition, mechanism, or immediate danger. This label/length correlation may teach abstention for brevity and cannot reliably establish the proposed positive severity label.
The label boundary depends on whether blood belongs to a person, injury depth, amount, whether bleeding stopped, and other symptoms. English/Tagalog/Cebuano code terms need human confirmation.

Distinguish a person pinned/trapped from a stuck door or vehicle part, severe crushing from non-crushing foot entrapment, physical inability to move from no description, and whether active hazards remain.

Lexical heuristics do not verify Cebuano idiom, Tagalog naturalness, regional usage, code-switch boundaries, or preservation of the clinical/operational meaning. Mixed-language tags were heuristic and need adjudication.

risk_findings.risk: Near-paraphrase/template leakage across nominally separate families
risk_findings.why: Within-language token overlap detects paraphrase-like pairs across separate family IDs. Similarity does not prove same event, but groups should be reviewed before split/evaluation because close templates across partitions can inflate held-out results.

length_label_shortcut_assessment.finding: Potential shortcut risk is present: the shortest length bucket is dominated by needs_review (34/54) and has few critical (5) or serious (8) examples. Dataset label totals and language totals are fairly balanced, but the length distribution is not balanced across labels or languages. A model may learn text length/report completeness as an abstention shortcut. Confirm with controlled human-reviewed evaluation and length-stratified metrics.

limitations: Regex and token Jaccard are mechanical screening only, not a Cebuano/Tagalog/English semantic validator.
No medical/responder label correctness is confirmed.
No model prediction or confidence was used for this audit.
Cross-family lexical similarity does not establish same incident; low lexical overlap does not establish distinct incidents.
training_or_deployment_recommendation: Do not infer that this corpus is semantically validated. Resolve high-priority text and family flags with fluent reviewers and responder adjudication before using a human-reviewed dataset for another training experiment.
